observations.explanation: The paper describes collecting API documentation from Torch Hub, TensorFlow Hub, and HuggingFace, and explains the filtering and GPT-4 self-instruct procedure used to create instruction–API pairs (pp. 2–4). The appendix adds dataset and task details (p. 13).

Table 1 reports Gorilla’s zero-shot accuracy as 71.68 on HuggingFace and 83.79 on TensorFlow Hub, higher than the listed comparison models; the table also shows different outcomes across retriever settings (p. 7).

The evaluation matches API calls and selected arguments using AST subtrees, rather than testing whether the generated code executes or completes the requested task (pp. 5–6). The appendix explicitly says execution results were not tested (p. 13).

The paper says the holdout set was made by splitting instruction–API pairs, but does not specify whether APIs themselves were held out, leaving API-level generalization unclear (p. 6; see also the split details on p. 13). It also explicitly states that for HuggingFace, all models except Gorilla are evaluated only for correct domain names, unlike the AST-based evaluation applied to Torch Hub and TensorFlow Hub (p. 7).
